newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus - Germany's MobilCom surges at bourse debut.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Germany's MobilCom surges at bourse debut.

text.p: MobilCom AG's stock surged more than 50 percent on its Frankfurt bourse debut on Monday, after demand for shares in Germany's largest independent mobile phone service provider exceeded supply 100 times over.
Originally issued at 62.50 marks, MobilCom shares ended their first trading day at 98 marks, outpacing the blue chip DAX index, which rose 1.8 percent.

The shares were issued as part of Germany's so-called New Market -- a highly publicised initiative modelled on New York's NASDAQ which is designed to promote share issues by innovative young companies.

Boosted by an intense spate of publicity, the 640,000-share MobilCom issue was oversubscribed 100 times over, its chief executive Gerhard Schmid told Reuters. Issue manager DG Bank later added that the greenshoe allocation of an additional 160,000 shares had been fully exercised.
Schmid said his company's shares had been priced at issue in order to leave room for substantial gains for investors.
He also said his five-year old firm, which develops products based on existing mobile phone networks, promised to show strong profit growth in the next few years, he said.

"The volume of (mobile phone) subscribers will increase dramatically in the years to come. And though prices will be declining, the margins for us will not decline. There will be economies of scale," Schmid told Reuters Financial Television.
MobilCom posted 12.1 million marks pre-tax profit in 1996 on sales of 309 million marks and has already predicted a 40 percent profit rise this year.
As a high-technology company, it is considered an ideal participant in the New Market system, which seeks to match risk-tolerant investors with suitable growth stocks.
Participants in the New Market receive help with public offerings, publicity and guaranteed liquidity in their stocks.

In return they must fulfil stringent issue and reporting requirements to offset the risk factor attached to them, including producing quarterly earnings reports and using International Accounting Standards.
Schmid said MobilCom opted for the scheme because of the publicity attached and because the tough reporting requirements matched his company's own philosophy on shareholder value.
